title: Properties of the strict w-local cover
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and let $C_A$ be the strict w-local cover algebra of [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. The map $A\to C_A$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Its spectrum is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], its local rings at maximal ideals are strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and the induced map from its closed points onto $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective.

proof.text: Put $W=A^w$, $E=W^{\mathrm e}$, $T=V(IE)$, and $C_A=E_{[T]}$, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. By [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points], the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}W$ form the closed subset $V(I)$ and map onto $\operatorname{Spec}A$: the point $(x,x)$ maps to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-contraction], $W\to E$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale and every maximal localization $E_q$ is strictly henselian.

We check that every $q\in T$ is maximal in $E$, rather than merely closed in a fibre. Its contraction $m=q\cap W$ contains $I$, so is a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}W$ and is maximal. The fibre $B=E\otimes_W\kappa(m)=E/mE$ is ind-etale by base-change stability [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], hence weakly etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], each finitely generated $\kappa(m)$-subalgebra of $B$ is finite etale. Thus every element of $B$ is algebraic over $\kappa(m)$: its powers lie in a finite-dimensional subalgebra. The domain $E/q$, a quotient of $B$, is consequently algebraic over $\kappa(m)$. For any nonzero $b\in E/q$, take a monic relation of least degree; its constant coefficient is nonzero, since otherwise cancellation of $b$ would give a shorter relation. Dividing the relation by $b$ expresses $b^{-1}$ as a polynomial in $b$. Hence $E/q$ is a field, and $q$ is maximal in $E$. This two-line algebraic-domain argument is written out here, not introduced as a new node.

The subset $T=V(IE)$ is Zariski closed and, by step 2, consists of closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization] with $R=E$ and this $T$. It gives $E\to C_A$ ind-Zariski, $\operatorname{Spec}C_A$ w-local, and its closed points identified with $T$. At the closed point corresponding to $q\in T$ the pair description is $(q,q)$, so the canonical local ring is $E_q$. Step 1 makes $E_q$ strictly henselian. Write this local-ring isomorphism as $\alpha:E_q\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_A)_{(q,q)}$. Restricting scalars along $\alpha$ makes each finite algebra over the latter ring a finite $E_q$-algebra, and its quotient by the maximal ideal is unchanged. Each idempotent in that quotient therefore has a unique lift by henselianity of $E_q$. The induced residue-field isomorphism makes the residue field separably closed. These are exactly the two conditions in [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Thus every maximal local ring of $C_A$ is strictly henselian.

For every $x\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, step 1 supplies a closed point $m$ of $\operatorname{Spec}W$ over $x$. Since $W\to E$ is faithfully flat, [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] supplies a prime $q$ of $E$ contracting to $m$. The inclusion $I\subseteq m$ implies $IE\subseteq q$, so $q\in T$. Step 3 identifies $q$ with a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}C_A$, whose image in $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is $q$ by the canonical pair description of [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is therefore $x$. This proves the claimed closed-point surjectivity.

By [def-weil-pbc-w-localization], $A\to W$ is ind-Zariski. The same holds for $E\to C_A$ by step 3, and $W\to E$ is ind-etale by step 1. Ind-Zariski is a special case of ind-etale in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Composition stability [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes $A\to C_A$ ind-etale, and that node also makes it weakly etale. In particular it is flat, by the flatness condition in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Step 4 makes the entire spectrum map surjective because its restriction to closed points already is. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] to conclude faithful flatness.
